subject: zoology
question_text: What is wish bone? What are the skeletal components that form it?

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack zoology section (book p.56, VSAQ 121). Zoology holds only ONE source book — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no zoology board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the back-test are both structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: What it is
steps.margin_note: Shape, other names, use. Three short lines.
lines: The wish bone is the V shaped bone in front of
It is also called the furcula or the merry
It acts as a spring and keeps the two wings
steps.why: The V shape is the reason the bone can spring back, so the shape and the use belong in the same breath.
common_mistakes: Calling the wish bone the sternum. The sternum is the breast bone; the wish bone lies in front of it.
Giving it to mammals. It is a bird character.
steps.memory_tip: A V that springs open and shut with every wing beat: the wish bone.

steps.label: What forms it
steps.margin_note: Name the three bones. One boxed line is enough for the mark.
lines: It is formed by the fusion of three bones.
So three bones fuse into one V shaped bone.
steps.why: The second half of the question asks for a bone list, so the count and the names are the whole mark and no description is needed.
common_mistakes: Naming only the clavicles. The interclavicle is the third bone and is part of the mark.
Writing that the ribs form it. The ribs take no part.
steps.memory_tip: Two collar bones plus the bone between them: three bones, one V.

insider_note: The question has two halves; the second half is a three bone list, and leaving out the interclavicle is the usual way students lose that mark.
